revision_rule.note: The 2012 rule states generally that size constraints precede iterative constraints; array-reduction constraints are categorized as iterative constraints in the following subclause.
The 2017 rule states the ordering for size constraints and iterative constraints generally, encompassing the following array-reduction iterative constraints subclause.
The 2012 random-variable rules do not state the later guarantee that associative-array size and index values are not randomizable.
IEEE 1800-2017 permits associative arrays to be random-qualified but does not state the later guarantee that their size and index values are nonrandomizable.
The 2012 declaration grammar permits optional static but has no dynamic override specifiers; the later initial, extends, and final constraint forms are absent.
The 2017 declaration grammar has optional static followed directly by constraint, identifier, and block; it does not admit the later dynamic override specifiers.

The 2012 Syntax 18-2 admits soft, implication, conditional, foreach, distribution, and disable-soft forms, but does not admit the later uniqueness constraint or default distribution-item alternatives.
The 2012 standard has no extends dynamic override specifier for constraints.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no extends dynamic override specifier for constraints.
The 2012 standard has no final specifier for constraints and therefore no corresponding prohibition on later replacement.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no final specifier for constraints and therefore no prohibition on replacing a constraint declared with it.
The 2012 standard has none of the final, initial, or extends dynamic constraint override specifiers.
IEEE 1800-2017 has none of the final, initial, or extends constraint override specifiers.
The 2017 restriction expressly prohibits output and ref arguments (allowing const ref), but does not include the later express prohibition on inout arguments.
IEEE 1800-2012 states this as a recommendation using “should”; the 2023 requirement makes automatic/stateless and side-effect-free behavior mandatory.
IEEE 1800-2017 states this as a should recommendation; IEEE 1800-2023 makes the stateless and side-effect-free behavior mandatory with shall.
The 2012 implication antecedent is restricted to an integral SystemVerilog expression; 2023 additionally permits a real expression.
IEEE 1800-2017 permits any integral antecedent expression, but does not include the later permission for a real antecedent.
The 2012 standard has neither initial nor extends constraint specifiers.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no initial or extends constraint override specifiers.
The 2012 standard has no initial constraint specifier or corresponding assertion that a declaration is not an override.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no initial constraint override specifier or its asserted non-override behavior.
In 2012 omission is allowed only when constraint_mode is called as a task; 2023 expresses the setter as a void function.
IEEE 1800-2017 permits omission of the name only on the task setter; the later standard replaces that setter task with a void function.
IEEE 1800-2012 defines the setter as a task and the query as a function, whereas 2023 defines void-function and integral-function overloads.
IEEE 1800-2017 defines the setter as a task rather than the later void function; the integral query form is otherwise present.
The 2012 constraint overview permits integral operands only and does not provide the later exception for nonrandom nonintegral operands yielding an integral or real result.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no exception allowing non-integral, non-real operands in a nonrandom subexpression producing an integral or real result.
The 2012 constraint_primary grammar has no optional empty-parentheses form; the later permission restricted to array built-in methods is absent.
IEEE 1800-2017 constraint_primary grammar does not include the later optional parentheses and associated array-built-in-only restriction.
The 2012 prototype and external-definition grammar supports qualifiers, static, scope, identifier, and block forms but has no dynamic override specifiers.
IEEE 1800-2017 provides extern/pure, static, class-scope, identifier, and block prototype forms but has no dynamic override specifiers.
IEEE 1800-2012 describes constraint operands as integral only; it does not permit real operands or the later nonrandom-subexpression exception.
IEEE 1800-2017 limits constraint expression variables and constants to integral types; it does not admit real operands or the later nonrandom-subexpression exception.
The 2012 disable-soft text does not state the later direct-appearance-only rule or distinguish a variable appearing in an enclosing hard portion.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not specify the later direct-appearance limitation distinguishing references inside soft expressions from enclosing hard portions.
The 2012 soft-constraint rules describe discarding preferences but do not specify the later constant-true replacement and no-distribution-effect guarantee.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not state the later replacement-by-true semantics and explicit absence of distribution effect for a discarded soft constraint.
The 2012 distribution grammar has no default distribution item.
IEEE 1800-2017 distribution syntax has no default item.
The 2012 distribution grammar has no default item denoting the complement of explicit items.
IEEE 1800-2017 distribution syntax has no default item or complement-range semantics.
The 2012 distribution grammar has no default distribution item or associated :/ requirement.
IEEE 1800-2017 distribution syntax has no default item.
The 2012 distribution rules do not specify that weights from overlapping or duplicate items are additive, including the later combined-zero behavior.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not specify the later additive treatment for a value occurring in multiple distribution items, including zero-weight occurrences.

IEEE 1800-2017 makes omitted values unavailable through set membership and treats an individual zero weight as a constraint, but does not define the later combined-weight treatment for duplicate occurrences.
The 2012 distribution set permits integral expressions and ranges only; real items and the mandatory :/ weight for real ranges are absent.
IEEE 1800-2017 distribution items and ranges are integral only; it has no real items or the mandatory :/ weight rule for real ranges.
The 2012 distribution rules permit integral values only and do not support mixing real and integral values.
IEEE 1800-2017 distributions support integral values and ranges only, not real values or mixed real/integral lists.
The 2012 distribution rules permit integral items only and have no real singleton weighting rule.
IEEE 1800-2017 distributions do not admit real singleton values.
The 2012 rule permits any integral SystemVerilog expression as a weight but does not specify the later unsigned interpretation of its result.
IEEE 1800-2017 permits any integral weight expression but does not specify the later unsigned interpretation of its result.
The 2012 distribution grammar supports value ranges with optional := or :/ weights but has no default distribution-item alternative.
IEEE 1800-2017 has expression, dist, value-range list, :=, and :/ forms but no default distribution item.
The 2012 standard has no initial, extends, or final constraint override specifiers to match between prototype and external block.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no initial, extends, or final constraint specifiers to match between a prototype and external block.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not state the later matching guarantee for static qualification of prototype/external pairs or pure-constraint overrides.
The 2012 foreach constraint rules do not state the later error for a function call used as an implicit variable declaration in the array identifier.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not state the later error rule for an implicit-variable-declaration function call in a constraint foreach identifier.
The 2012 foreach constraint rules describe arrays but do not define a string as a dynamic byte array for constraint iteration.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not define a string as a dynamic byte array for constraint foreach iteration.
The 2012 if-else constraint condition may be any integral expression; the later rule additionally permits real expressions.
IEEE 1800-2017 permits any integral condition expression but does not include the later permission for real conditions.
IEEE 1800-2017 defines inside as set membership but does not state the later equal-probability guarantee for all satisfying values.
The 2012 set-membership constraint rules support integer value sets and do not permit real-valued inside ranges.
IEEE 1800-2017 constraint set membership does not permit the later real-valued range behavior.
The 2012 random-variable rules do not define the later randomization classification and member restriction for packed untagged unions.
The 2012 random-variable rules do not state the later prohibition on rand or randc packed tagged unions.
The 2012 random-variable rules do not state the later prohibition on rand or randc unpacked unions.
The 2012 random-variable rules do not support real random variables and have no corresponding real-specific randc prohibition.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not permit real variables to be random-qualified and therefore has no later rand-versus-randc distinction for real variables.
The 2012 random-variable rules do not define the later integral-treatment enum exception for rand packed structures and packed untagged unions.
The 2012 standard has no final constraint specifier and therefore no pure-constraint combination prohibition.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no final constraint specifier and therefore no pure-constraint prohibition involving it.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not state the later rule requiring an override to match a pure constraint's static qualification.
In 2012 omission is allowed only when rand_mode is called as a task; 2023 expresses the setter as a void function.
IEEE 1800-2017 permits omission only on the task setter; the later standard replaces that setter task with a void function.
IEEE 1800-2012 defines the setter as a task and the query as a function, whereas 2023 defines void-function and integral-function overloads.
IEEE 1800-2017 defines the setter as a task rather than the later void function; the integral query is otherwise present.
The 2012 random-variable rules do not support rand real variables or define uniform probability over real subranges.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not support rand real variables or define a uniform distribution over their constraint-defined ranges.
The 2012 randomization overview does not state the later rule limiting active random enum variables to named constants while allowing unnamed enum state values.
The 2012 random-variable rules do not define whole packed structures as rand or randc variables randomized as integral types.
The 2012 random-variable rules do not define whole packed untagged unions as rand or randc variables randomized as integral types.
The 2012 random-stability list covers $urandom/$urandom_range, srandom, and object randomize, but does not list shuffle, randcase, randsequence, or scope randomize in this domain statement.
IEEE 1800-2012 states that the solver can randomize singular variables of integral type; real types are not included.
IEEE 1800-2017 permits solver randomization of singular integral types only; real types were added later.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not specify preservation of retained-element rand_mode or activation of new elements during dynamic-array or queue resizing.
The 2012 rule permits array.size as an ordering variable but does not permit the later parenthesized array.size() form.
IEEE 1800-2017 permits array.size as an ordering variable but does not include the later optional parenthesized array.size() form.
The 2012 solve-before grammar has the same list structure but constraint_primary has no optional parentheses for array built-in methods.
IEEE 1800-2017 has the same solve-list-before-list structure but constraint_primary does not have the later optional array-built-in parentheses.
The 2012 ordering rule permits integral variables only; real-valued solve-before variables are not included.
IEEE 1800-2017 restricts solve-before variables to integral values; real values were added later.
The 2012 standard has no dynamic constraint override specifiers and therefore no static-combination prohibition.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no dynamic constraint override specifiers and therefore no prohibition on combining them with static constraints.
IEEE 1800-2012 explicitly guarantees thread-execution-order independence for $urandom; the 2023 rule extends the guarantee to $urandom_range, scope randomize, shuffle, randcase, and randsequence.
The 2012 rule guarantees stable size only for an unconstrained dynamic array; it does not include queues or the later case where all size constraints are discarded soft constraints.
The 2012 unique group permits integral scalar variables and unpacked arrays or slices with integral leaves; real singular variables and real leaf types are not permitted.
IEEE 1800-2017 permits integral scalar variables and unpacked arrays or slices with integral leaves; real variables and real leaf types were added later.
IEEE 1800-2017 uses a restricted open_range_list and permits only scalar integral variables or unpacked arrays/slices with integral leaves; the later grammar and admitted real forms differ.
